answer: No. A baked section is a stored Markdown snapshot, so it doesn't refresh by itself, and you have to update the baked section when you want to refresh it. Only live queries re-evaluate when their data changes.

## If the data behind a query I froze into the page as plain Markdown changes, does the frozen copy update on its own?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Guide/Aggregator Pages.md] ---
### Keep a portable copy

# Keep a portable copy
Live queries render in SilverBullet. Use [[Baked Sections]] if you also need stored Markdown that other tools can display. Update the baked section when you want to refresh that snapshot.

[[Workbench/Data]] documents the builder controls. [[Object Index]] explains the available query sources.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/ADR/003 Indexed Object Graph.md] ---
### Context

# Context
SilverBullet’s power features — [[Space Lua/Integrated Query]], [[Linked Mention]], the [[Linked Tasks]], [[Graph View]] — all need *structured, queryable* data. But the source of truth is plain markdown files. Something needs to turn that prose into queryable data without making the markdown any less plain.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Guide/When Results Update.md] ---
### After editing a page

# After editing a page
SilverBullet saves the Markdown and updates its [[Object Index]] asynchronously. A query reads indexed records, so a new task or changed attribute can take a moment to appear. Live expressions track their dependencies and reevaluate when relevant data changes. This is not a guarantee that every widget polls every external resource.

After changing data used by a query, allow saving and indexing to settle. Its result updates without rebuilding the query or running `System: Reload`.

Search has its own index and startup behavior. [[Search#The search index]] explains when text search may still be catching up.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Markdown.md] ---
### Untitled

Markdown uses plain text to mark headings, lists, emphasis and links. SilverBullet renders that formatting while you write, and keeps the source in ordinary `.md` files.

Completely new to markdown? Start with [[Guide/My First Markdown Page]] for a short exercise, or use [[Markdown/Basics]] as a syntax reference.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Guide/Reading These Docs.md] ---
### Try a copied example

# Try a copied example
In your own pace, press **Cmd-k** on macOS or **Ctrl-k** on Windows/Linux, type `Markdown Practice`, and press **Shift-Enter**. Paste the block above into the page body. Move your cursor away to see a heading and an unchecked task. Click the checkbox to mark it complete. Your practice page changes, while this documentation stays unchanged.
